playbook.intent: An agent builder needs the corpus available to a retrieval bot, an outbound assistant or a code-review agent, and the only route on offer is scraping markdown written for human eyes out of a command-line tool. It is over when the agent reads typed records across a pinned contract instead, and each claim it emits carries a citation token that resolves back to the exact document behind it.
playbook.scope: Agent builder wires faion CLI as a structured methodology lookup inside their agent (RAG-as-a-service / SDR / code-review bot) without parsing human-readable markdown, and emits faion-citation tokens in agent output.

success-criteria.criterion: Nothing in the integration parses prose written for human readers: every field the agent consumes arrives as typed data against a declared schema
A lookup reads the manifest first and pulls full document bodies only for the entries the agent decided it needed
Tool failures return as typed error values the caller can branch on, plainly distinguishable from an empty but successful result
Fetched bodies are dropped from the working window once they have been used, so a long-running session does not accumulate everything it ever read
The schema version travels in the call, and a corpus update that changes shape shows up as an explicit mismatch instead of silently shifting the agent's answers
Stable prefixes sit ahead of the variable lookup in the assembled prompt, with the cache-hit rate measured before and after to prove the ordering earned its place
Each claim in the agent's output carries a citation token a reader can follow back to the source document and the version it was read at
